question: Does AR(1) forecast the terminal Cooling and Excess scores better than climatology and a constant 0.5? (forecast quality only; pricing evaluated separately)

specification.source: macropaths-maths.md section 5 (walk-forward, proper scoring rules, coverage, randomised PIT) and section 6.3 (asking policy); research/README.md and research/build_notebook.py (cap rule)
specification.fit: OLS y_{t+1} = a + b y_t + e on observations dated HIST_START .. t0-1 (macrolib.fit_ou(until=t0-1); its slice includes `until`)
specification.simulation: 10000 paths x 48 months from x0 = y_(t0-1); Gaussian innovations with the fitted residual sd (ddof=2); x0 not part of the contract path
specification.quantisation: simulated percent -> floor(y * 1e4) contract units, then the exact integer recursions and scores of eqs. (2)-(6)
specification.climatology: realised scores of every 48-month window that ended <= t0-1, from HIST_START
specification.crps: empirical-distribution CRPS: mean|X-y| - sum_i (2i-n-1) X_(i) / n^2 (pair term normalised 1/(2n^2)); 'fair' 1/(2n(n-1)) reported alongside
specification.pit: randomised PIT u = F(y-) + v (F(y) - F(y-)), seeded v
specification.decision_rule:
Declared before running: a winner needs the 95% block-bootstrap CI of the mean CRPS
    difference to exclude 0 on the same side for every L in (24, 48, 96), seed-to-seed spread of
    the mean difference below 10% of its size, and the same sign in the non-overlapping origins.
specification.policy_A: fixed caps 8 pp / 80 pp-months: RETROSPECTIVE DEMONSTRATION (caps chosen after seeing 2021-24), not a pre-specified evaluation
specification.policy_B: pre-origin percentile caps, rule below; applied to simulated, realised and climatology scores at the same origin

cap_rule.statistic: 90th percentile of the exact integer statistic over eligible 48-month windows
cap_rule.eligible_windows: start >= 1960-01 (declared post-1960 rule) and end <= t0 - 1
cap_rule.interpolation: linear between order statistics (Hyndman-Fan type 7; numpy 'linear', the pandas Series.quantile default used by research/build_notebook.py)
cap_rule.rounding: round half up to an integer in contract units (declared here: the repo has no integer rounding rule)
cap_rule.no_valid_cap: a percentile <= 0 gives no valid cap (the program needs cap > 0 and the notebook skips such products): that product is excluded from policy B at that origin and counted
cap_rule.source: research/README.md ('p90 ... post-1960 (or series-start) windows'), research/build_notebook.py (CAP_WINDOW_START = 1960-01, stats.quantile(0.9))

settings.seed_streams: SeedSequence([seed, purpose, year*12+month]); purposes: 0 simulation, 1 PIT, 2 bootstrap

A/cooling.status: holds in none of the 4 variants

B/cooling.status: holds in none of the 4 variants

variant_notes.primary: Gaussian innovations, AR(1) fit and climatology from 1914-01 (declared before running)
variant_notes.iid residuals: innovations resampled i.i.d. from the fitted residuals (fat tails kept)
variant_notes.12-month block residuals: innovations resampled in blocks of 12 consecutive residuals (keeps within-year residual dependence, the lag-12 check)
variant_notes.history from 1960: AR(1) fit and climatology both start at 1960-01; policy B caps unchanged
variant_notes.fit window 288 months: AR(1) fitted on the last 288 months before each origin (1997-01..2020-12 at the 2021-01 origin); climatology from 1914. Added after the 2021-01 cross-check showed the maths note's reference V0 matches a 1997-2020 fit; not part of the declared rule

pricing_policy.policy: p = clamp(V + kappa*sigma, 0.05, 0.95), V and sigma = AR(1) mean and sd of the score at the origin; per unit of cover: buyer pays p, receives y; seller result = buyer net cost = p - y (zero-sum per unit, collateral returned)

maths_note_reference_V0.note: reviewer's run, 50,000 paths, AR(1) on pre-2021 data, macropaths-maths.md section 5

jan2021.finding: The maths note's V0 (about 0.32 / 0.009) is not reproduced by the primary fit from 1914 (world-war volatility roughly doubles the residual sd). It is reproduced by an AR(1) fitted on 1997-01..2020-12, the '288 months' variant. research/build_notebook.py fits on all history (fit_ou default), as the primary does, so 'pre-2021 data' is ambiguous in the sources.

effective_sample.note: consecutive origins share 47 of 48 months; the evaluation holds roughly 14.0 independent 48-month blocks

conclusion: Cooling, pre-origin caps (the honest test): climatology beats AR(1). Mean CRPS AR(1) 0.2004 vs climatology 0.1655 vs constant 0.2907; mean difference +0.0349, 95% block-bootstrap CI (L=48) [+0.0129, +0.0634]; non-overlapping origins: AR(1) better in 6 of 15. Specification variants: holds in none of the 4 variants (not significant with iid residuals, 12-month block residuals, history from 1960, fit window 288 months).

Excess, pre-origin caps (the honest test): AR(1) beats climatology. Mean CRPS AR(1) 0.0913 vs climatology 0.1626 vs constant 0.4569; mean difference -0.0712, 95% block-bootstrap CI (L=48) [-0.1218, -0.0243]; non-overlapping origins: AR(1) better in 12 of 14. Specification variants: holds in 3 of 4 variants (not significant with 12-month block residuals).

Cooling, fixed caps 8/80 (retrospective): climatology beats AR(1). Mean CRPS AR(1) 0.2647 vs climatology 0.2165 vs constant 0.2388; mean difference +0.0481, 95% block-bootstrap CI (L=48) [+0.0221, +0.0732]; non-overlapping origins: AR(1) better in 4 of 15. Specification variants: holds in none of the 4 variants (not significant with iid residuals, 12-month block residuals, history from 1960, fit window 288 months).

Excess, fixed caps 8/80 (retrospective): AR(1) beats climatology. Mean CRPS AR(1) 0.1652 vs climatology 0.2285 vs constant 0.4073; mean difference -0.0633, 95% block-bootstrap CI (L=48) [-0.1260, -0.0203]; non-overlapping origins: AR(1) better in 10 of 15. Specification variants: holds in 3 of 4 variants (not significant with 12-month block residuals).

Cooling: no convincing winner. The primary specification gives 'climatology beats AR(1)', but it holds in none of the 4 specification variants, so the result depends on modelling choices (Gaussian innovations, fit from 1914) rather than on a stable difference in skill.
Excess: AR(1) beats climatology (holds in 3 of 4 variants); the evidence is moderately convincing given about 14 independent 48-month blocks.
Calibration: the primary AR(1) over-forecasts Cooling (policy B: 57% of randomised PITs fall in the lowest decile, against 10% for a calibrated forecast).
Calibration: the primary AR(1) over-forecasts Excess (policy B: 22% of randomised PITs fall in the lowest decile, against 10% for a calibrated forecast).

Specification finding: The maths note's V0 (about 0.32 / 0.009) is not reproduced by the primary fit from 1914 (world-war volatility roughly doubles the residual sd). It is reproduced by an AR(1) fitted on 1997-01..2020-12, the '288 months' variant. research/build_notebook.py fits on all history (fit_ou default), as the primary does, so 'pre-2021 data' is ambiguous in the sources.

Pricing (separate from forecast quality): with κ = 0.5 under policy B the seller's mean result per unit would have been cooling +0.301, excess +0.205. A positive result here mostly reflects quotes set from a forecast that runs high, not a validated policy. The policy needs re-evaluating with a calibrated forecast before any quote is called reliable.
The evidence rests on about 14.0 independent 48-month blocks, so even large average differences carry wide uncertainty; the block-bootstrap intervals above are the honest measure.

Next research step: fix the AR(1) fit window in the specification (all history vs a rolling 24 years), then evaluate the maths note's alternative 2 (a model of monthly inflation with year-on-year reconstructed by summation, which respects the lag-12 overlap and the fat-tailed residuals) on this same harness, and widen the evaluation set (other CPI measures or countries) to raise the effective sample size.
